rule: An item is accepted when at least one of the three reviewers accepts it and none asks for a change or rejects it. One 'change' or 'reject' holds it until that reviewer accepts. All three are asked to read; one acceptance is enough to go on (owner decision of 7 October 2026).

items.check: Read the result. items.title: The stability of the SE1 classes over all 180 cells
items.check: Read the result. The other 90 cells of the uncertainty ensemble were run, report-only, with the 2020 resident counts rescaled to 2024 totals. Over the 180 cells seven of the eight tambons keep their class, Ko Chang in 78 percent. Mae Sai town keeps class D in 50 percent, under the 60 percent the protocol asks: it is D with the 2020 counts and A, B or C with the rescaled counts. Nothing published changes. Accept if the team agrees with the two readings of the rescale (a count belongs to the 1 km cell that holds its centre; a count with no 2024 total keeps its 2020 value) and will say in the pitch that the town's class depends on the population product. Whether the result file is published again with a status on each class is a separate decision of the owners.
items.gates: Saying how stable a class of case SE1 is, in the pitch or on a page.

items.title: Access loss by age: over the 180 cells, with a smallest size, and with registered age counts
items.check: Read the three sections added on 9 and 11 October. With the modelled age grid, over the 180 cells, the differences between age groups are small; the owners state a gap only from one percentage point, so no gap is stated for the district. With the registered age mix of each tambon (DOPA, December 2024) the direction turns round, and it holds in all 180 cells: residents of 60 and over lose hospital access at 1.06 to 1.13 times the rate of younger residents. The registered ages leave out two registered residents in five, who are not Thai nationals. Accept if the team will say that the direction of the age gap depends on the age data, will give both readings with their limits, and will not lead the pitch with the equity gap.
